_nota: Fuente: George S. Clason, The Richest Man in Babylon (1926), capítulo 'The Richest Man in Babylon' (Bansir y Arkad, 'a part of all you earn is yours to keep... not less than a tenth').
babi01-bansir: an ancient Babylonian craftsman building a wooden chariot wheel in a dusty workshop, tired face, warm sunset light through the door
babi02-arkad: a wealthy old Babylonian man in rich embroidered robes sitting in a palace garden with palm trees and fountains, golden light
babi03-pregunta: two ancient Babylonian men talking face to face in a courtyard of blue glazed bricks, dramatic side light
babi04-diez: ten ancient gold coins on a stone table, one coin separated from the others and glowing, dramatic light
babi05-pagate: an ancient hand dropping a gold coin into a clay jar, other coins inside, warm lamp light
babi06-nueve: an ancient Babylonian family eating dinner together at a simple table, happy, oil lamps, warm light
babi07-jarra: a clay jar overflowing with gold coins on a wooden shelf, a ray of sunlight from a window
babi08-trabajar: golden coins multiplying and growing like plants in an ancient Babylonian garden, magical realism, warm light
babi09-libro: an old leather bound book lying on a table next to ancient gold coins and a clay tablet, candlelight
babi10-final: the Ishtar gate of Babylon with blue glazed bricks at golden hour, epic wide view
